description_good_justification: https://vcon-server.com/ says what it does: it stores vCons, the IETF format for conversation records, encrypted at rest, and returns them only to the keys allowed to see them.
interact_justification: How to obtain it: https://vcon-server.com/docs/getting-started/ . How to report bugs, ask for features and contribute: https://vcon-server.com/docs/development/#contributing .
contribution_justification: Changes come as GitHub pull requests against main, with the repository hooks enabled and the CLA signed: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md requires a test written first for each change, reserved test data only, the hooks (cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests) and the CLA.
floss_license_justification: MIT OR Apache-2.0, at the user's option: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/LICENSE-MIT and https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/LICENSE-APACHE .
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT and Apache-2.0 are both OSI-approved.
license_location_justification: LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT in the repository root, and the same texts named by SPDX identifier in https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/tree/main/LICENSES (REUSE layout).
documentation_basics_justification: Install, start and use: https://vcon-server.com/docs/getting-started/ . Secure use: https://vcon-server.com/docs/security/ and https://vcon-server.com/docs/operations/ .
documentation_interface_justification: HTTP API: https://vcon-server.com/docs/http-api/ . Command line: https://vcon-server.com/docs/command-line/ . Configuration file: https://vcon-server.com/docs/configuration/ . Problem documents: https://vcon-server.com/problems/ . OpenAPI 3.1 description: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/crates/vcon-server/openapi.json
sites_https_justification: https://vcon-server.com (HTTP answers 301 to HTTPS) and https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server are served over HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues, pull requests and discussions: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/issues and https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/discussions . They are searchable, addressable by URL, open to anyone with a GitHub account and need no proprietary client.
english_justification: The documentation, the code comments and the issue tracker are in English; CONTRIBUTING.md asks for issues in English.
maintained_justification: Under active development; commits land on main every few days: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/commits/main
repo_track_justification: Git records each change, its author and its date.
repo_interim_justification: Every change is committed to main, not only releases: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/commits/main
version_unique_justification: Each release has its own version: v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 so far (https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/releases). The release workflow refuses a v* tag that is not v plus the Cargo.toml version: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
version_semver_justification: Versions follow Semantic Versioning, as https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md states; the current version is 0.2.0 (Cargo.toml).
version_tags_justification: Each release is a v* git tag (v0.1.0, v0.2.0), and the release workflow publishes only from a pushed v* tag: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md is a human-readable summary in Keep a Changelog form, not a git log, with a section for each release (0.1.0, 0.2.0), each linked to its GitHub release.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability: there is no security advisory (https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/security/advisories) and no CVE for this project. The 0.1.0 notes' Security section records a stack-overflow fix made before the first release.
report_process_justification: Bugs and feature requests are GitHub issues, as https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md and https://vcon-server.com/docs/development/#contributing describe: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/issues
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been submitted since the repository was created on 2026-10-24: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been submitted since the repository was created on 2026-10-24: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues are public and searchable: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is on for the repository, as https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/SECURITY.md says: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received.
build_justification: Cargo builds the whole workspace from source: cargo build --release (https://vcon-server.com/docs/getting-started/).
build_common_tools_justification: Cargo, the standard Rust build tool.
build_floss_tools_justification: The build needs only FLOSS tools: Rust, Cargo, a C compiler, make and perl.
test_justification: cargo test --workspace, documented in https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/README.md and https://vcon-server.com/docs/development/ , runs in CI on every push and pull request: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_invocation_justification: cargo test, the standard Rust invocation.
test_most_justification: CI's coverage job measures the tests with cargo-llvm-cov on every push. On commit 54318ec they covered 98.48% of lines (17,959 of 18,237) and 97.76% of functions: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/actions/runs/40677322608/job/122778944126 . https://vcon-server.com/ publishes the same figures from CI.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs fmt, clippy and the tests on every push to main and every pull request: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md: each change comes with the test that encodes it, written first and seen failing for the right reason.
tests_are_added_justification: For example, the change that added GET /vcons added 25 tests with it: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/commit/d20c046a79123399df5c420efbe5e8a23609aa71
warnings_justification: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check run in the commit hook (https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.githooks/pre-commit) and in CI (https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml). The web console's JavaScript is an ES module, so it runs in strict mode.
warnings_fixed_justification: -D warnings makes every rustc and clippy warning an error, so a change with a warning fails the hook and CI; main builds with none: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/actions/runs/40677322608
warnings_strict_justification: Every rustc and clippy warning is an error, on every target including the tests and the examples.
crypto_published_justification: Only published, reviewed algorithms: AES-256-GCM, HKDF-SHA256, SHA-256, TLS 1.2 and 1.3, SQLCipher 4: https://vcon-server.com/docs/security/
crypto_call_justification: All cryptography is called from AWS-LC (through aws-lc-rs), rustls and SQLCipher; vcon-server implements none itself.
crypto_floss_justification: AWS-LC, aws-lc-rs, rustls, SQLCipher community edition and OpenSSL are all FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: Every key the server makes is 256 bits. TLS uses rustls's defaults with AWS-LC: AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305, with X25519, P-256, P-384 or X25519MLKEM768 key agreement. The configuration has no TLS version or cipher setting, so none of this can be lowered; the TLS certificate and its key are the operator's.
crypto_working_justification: No MD4, MD5, DES, RC4 or Dual_EC_DRBG. Every encryption is AES-256-GCM with a random 96-bit nonce; SQLCipher 4 pages are AES-256-CBC authenticated with HMAC-SHA512.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 and no unauthenticated CBC: hashes are SHA-256 or stronger, and TLS uses AEAD suites only.
crypto_pfs_justification: TLS through rustls offers TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2 ECDHE suites only, so every session key is ephemeral.
crypto_password_storage_justification: vcon-server stores no passwords. API tokens hold a 256-bit random secret made by the server, and only the token's SHA-256 is kept.
crypto_random_justification: Every key, nonce and token secret comes from AWS-LC's CSPRNG through aws_lc_rs::rand (fill, and generate with SystemRandom): https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/crates/vcon-server/src/envelope.rs
delivery_mitm_justification: The source is fetched from GitHub over HTTPS or SSH. Release files come with SHA256SUMS.txt and Sigstore build provenance, checked with gh attestation verify (https://vcon-server.com/docs/getting-started/).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is fetched over HTTP. CI checks every downloaded tool against a sha256 written in the workflow; release files carry signed build provenance.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There is no publicly known vulnerability: no security advisory (https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/security/advisories) and no open Dependabot alert.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been reported. https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/SECURITY.md sets 30 days as the target for fixing a critical problem.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No private key, password or token is committed. GitHub secret scanning and push protection are on and have no alerts; the tests make their keys and certificates at run time.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript for the web console, and GitHub Actions) on every push, every pull request and weekly: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml . Clippy runs in every commit hook and CI run.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security queries for Rust look for common vulnerabilities such as cleartext logging of secrets and hard-coded cryptographic values.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No static-analysis finding has been an exploitable vulnerability. Of CodeQL's alerts, one was fixed, and each other was dismissed as a false positive or as test-only code, with its reason recorded.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every push and pull request and weekly; clippy runs on every commit: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Fuzzing and property tests on every push and pull request. cargo-fuzz targets (https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/tree/main/fuzz/fuzz_targets) run for 60 seconds each in CI and must find a panic planted in the code they read; ClusterFuzzLite fuzzes pull requests, pushes to main and every target weekly (https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/clusterfuzzlite.yml). proptest feeds generated inputs to the vCon reader: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/crates/vcon/tests/properties.rs
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: vcon-server's tests run under AddressSanitizer, with the standard library rebuilt instrumented, and the locked-memory page's tests under Miri, on every pull request and push that changes crates/ and every week: https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/sanitizers.yml . The fuzz targets also run under AddressSanitizer, in CI and in ClusterFuzzLite (https://github.com/NormB/vcon-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/clusterfuzzlite.yml).
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: cargo test builds the dev profile, with debug assertions and integer-overflow checks on; the workspace sets no profile that turns them off.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic-analysis finding has been confirmed as an exploitable vulnerability.
